central_question: Question 5.9 (paper label question:super_omega_cluster): Is there a function ell such that for every tournament T, if omega_vec(T) >= k then T has a subtournament A with |A| <= ell(k) and omega_vec(A) >= k?  Here omega_vec(T) is the clique number of the tournament = min over all total orders prec of V(T) of the ordinary clique number omega(T^prec) of the backedge graph T^prec (edge uv iff u prec v and the arc v->u is backward). This is the STRONG f=identity form of Conjecture 5.8 (conj:omega_omega_cluster: large omega_vec implies an omega_vec-cluster). Its NEGATION is Conjecture 5.10 (conj:critique): for every k>=3 there are infinitely many k-omega_vec-critical tournaments (omega_vec(T)=k and omega_vec(T-v)=k-1 for every vertex v). Conjecture 5.10 true => Question 5.9 answered NO; Conjecture 5.10 false => Question 5.9 answered YES.

benchmark.description: The fixed exact yardstick. omega_vec is computed EXACTLY (no heuristics): brute force over n! orders for n<=7, exact branch-and-bound (identical value, cross-checked) above. For vertex-transitive (circulant) tournaments the whole-tournament omega_vec is reachable past the unrestricted-bb wall via a SOUND symmetry-reduced bb (fix an orbit-representative vertex first; the automorphism group acts on total orders so the global min is attained by an order starting at that vertex). Every proposed tournament is GROUNDED against the oracle before any reasoning is trusted.
benchmark.invariant: omega_vec(T) = min_{prec in S(V(T))} omega(T^prec); backedge graph T^prec has edge uv iff u prec v and v->u in A(T).

min_subtournament_order_for_k(T,k): smallest |X| of a subtournament X with omega_vec(X)>=k (the ell(k) certificate of Question 5.9).
